title: Matrixed latency-capacity orchestrator for regional routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region outages or capacity pressure we need a routing policy that simultaneously respects per-customer latency SLOs, preserves cost/throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers, and avoids islanding traffic into overloaded regions. Existing steering policies either prioritize pure latency (which can cause capacity collapse) or hard geo-pinning (which sacrifices global SLOs).

Proposal summary: Implement a Matrixed Latency-Capacity Orchestrator (MLCO) that combines three signals: latency budget headroom, region capacity credits, and geo-affinity score. The MLCO computes a per-request region preference vector and a soft-eviction plan. It emits per-request routing hints with a graded fallback order and associated shed probability. Routing decisions are probabilistic and credit-weighted so that we achieve graceful load shedding instead of hard failovers.

Key features: 
- Latency Budgeting: Each customer-route has a rolling latency budget (e.g., 99th percentile budget over 10m). Requests with low headroom are marked "latency-critical" and are steered preferentially to low-latency regions.
- Capacity Credits: Regions expose tokenized credits scoped by model-class and tenancy (shared or dedicated). Credits are consumed per-started-request and replenish on completion. Credits throttle selection probability for a region rather than absolute blocking.
- Geo Affinity TTL: Customers can be geo-pinned with an affinity score and a TTL. The orchestrator respects affinity by biasing probabilities but will overrule affinity under sustained capacity shortfall to maintain global SLOs.
- Tokenized Circuit Breakers: Circuit breakers operate on credit depletion trajectories. Instead of rigid open/closed, we use a 4-state tokenized breaker (Healthy / Soft-Tripped / Hard-Tripped / Recovering) with graduated shedding and retry-backoff multipliers.
- Soft Eviction & Leaky-Bucket Shedding: When region load exceeds a threshold, MLCO applies soft eviction using leaky-bucket shedding where lower-priority requests (e.g., background embeddings, large-context generations) accept higher shed probability. Sampling is deterministic per-request using request fingerprint + conductor seed for reproducibility.
- Observability & Safety: Expose per-customer/regional metrics (credit balance, latency budget headroom, breaker state), and a simulated-timeline endpoint to preview routing under hypothetical outages.

Rollout plan: 
1) Canary-only simulation (2 weeks): implement MLCO in the simulator service, replay recent 30 days of traffic, and measure predictive SLO retention and shed rates.
2) Shadow mode (1 week): MLCO computes hints for production traffic but does not control routing; collect decision vs actual outcome traces.
3) Partial rollout (2 weeks): Enable routing for a small customer cohort (10% traffic) with conservative credit thresholds and global canary throttles.
4) Full rollout (after 4 weeks of monitoring + safety signoffs).

Metrics to track: 
- SLO retention by customer (P50/P95/P99 latency) pre/post route decision.
- Shed rate (requests and tokens) by region and by customer tier.
- Credit churn and replenishment latency.
- Breaker state transitions frequency and mean time to recover.
- Error and retry amplification (to detect feedback loops).

Trade-offs and open questions: 
- Complexity vs debuggability: MLCO's probabilistic decisions are harder to reason about in realtime than deterministic pin-and-failover. We'll mitigate with deterministic fingerprinting and a replayable decision log.
- Dedicated capacity vs shared fairness: Need policy to guarantee minimum reserved region capacity for Dedicated pools. Proposal: region credits have a reserved pool that is only consumed after shared pool crosses a threshold.
- Cost: probabilistic routing may increase egress/latency costs when routing to farther regions; we will surface cost impact per customer in Console before wider rollout.

Safety checks required before merge: 
- Chaos test in staging with an injected 30% capacity drop in the primary region. 
- End-to-end integration test for tokenized breakers (deterministic sequences).
- Console panel with kill-switch and per-customer override.

Expected outcome: Reduced P99 SLO violations during cross-region perturbations by 40% and reduced full hard-failover incidents by 60%, at the expense of controlled shedding of non-critical workloads.
